novcanik.qr_opis: Show this code to receive POEN. Scan with phone.
novcanik.opis_stranice: Your POEN ledger — how much has been recorded for you and what has happened. POEN records your contribution; it is not money and cannot be exchanged for dinars. From here you can re-register POEN to another member.
novcanik.prazno_naslov: You don't have any POEN recorded yet.
novcanik.prazno_opis: POEN is recorded through community participation — through confirmation, exchanging goods and services, or making contributions. Start by getting confirmed.
novcanik.zabelezen_opis: It is recorded once the Foundation approves your first listing, once someone confirms you, or once someone re-registers POEN into your record. Until then it is not a POEN record and does not count towards your balance.
novcanik.samo_primalac: Until you are confirmed you can only receive POEN. Re-registering POEN into someone else's record opens up upon confirmation.
novcanik.nadoknada_opis: It arose from the annulment of a false confirmation you performed. It is not a debt and cannot be collected — POEN you receive fill it first. Exchange of goods and services is not restricted; re-registering POEN to someone else becomes possible once your record passes zero.
novcanik.putanja_opis: Five steps, 1,000 POEN each. They unlock in order, and no user is recorded more than 5,000 POEN in total.
novcanik.putanja_korak_1: First listing offering a good or a service that meets the content minimum
novcanik.putanja_korak_2: First exchange in which you re-register POEN to a user outside your chain
novcanik.putanja_korak_3: Three listings, two of which received an enquiry from different users
novcanik.putanja_korak_4: Exchanges with 5 different people outside your chain
novcanik.putanja_korak_5: Exchanges with 10 different people outside your chain
novcanik.putanja_zabelezen: Noted — the record follows approval or confirmation
novcanik.putanja_pravila: The count includes re-registrations of at least 1,000 POEN with people outside your circle of acquaintance (the network of confirmations). Each counterpart counts once, however many re-registrations there are. A re-registration with a user who is not yet confirmed is noted, but counts only once they are confirmed. Currently counted: {sagovornika}.

landing.meta_title: KOLO — an exchange system you build with your community
landing.meta_desc: KOLO is a network for exchanging work, goods and knowledge — what some have is what others need.
landing.hero_naslov: An exchange network you build in your own community
landing.hero_podnaslov: Work, goods and knowledge circulate among people where you live — no middlemen, no money.
landing.problem_1_naslov: Food travels, while it grows right next to us.
landing.problem_1_opis: We buy honey, eggs, cheese and vegetables that have crossed thousands of kilometres, while someone in the neighbourhood produces exactly that.
landing.problem_1_poenta: What we need grows right next to us, yet never reaches us.
landing.problem_2_naslov: The producer has no one to sell to.
landing.problem_2_opis: What's left is a buyer who dictates the price, or a market stall you stand at all day. A small producer can't break into the big chains: they are shut out of them, and we are shut inside them.
landing.problem_2_poenta: The demand exists, the supply exists, the channel doesn't.
landing.problem_3_opis: The neighbour is a skilled tradesman, the woman next door makes the best cheese around, their son gives lessons. And only the people closest to them know it.
landing.problem_3_poenta: What we need every day, no one brings together in one place.
landing.alternativa_naslov: KOLO is a well we dig together
landing.alternativa_citat:
When people were thirsty, together they dug a well.
Everyone drank from it, and no one was thirsty any more.
The well was no one's property, yet it was everyone's care: they agreed how it would be used and maintained it themselves.
That is why it lasted.
landing.alternativa_podnaslov: KOLO is that well. You do not draw water from it — you exchange what people can do and what they have.
landing.alternativa_1_opis: A neighbour, a friend, a friend of a friend, and then someone from the next village you don't know yet. What some have is what others need, and that is exactly what brings them together. Every exchange is one connection that did not exist before.
landing.alternativa_2_opis_start: Every time you give someone in the network work, goods or knowledge, it is recorded. That record is called a
landing.alternativa_2_opis_end: , the network's unit of account. It is not money, it is not exchanged for dinars, it is not traded on any market. A POEN shows what you have given to the community, and that is how people come to know you.
landing.alternativa_3_naslov: The rules are the same for everyone
landing.alternativa_3_opis: The rules of the system and the way decisions are made are written down and anyone can read them. They are not changed in favour of an individual, but together and by the same procedure for everyone. Shared resources are governed by the community itself, not by someone on the outside.
landing.kome_1_opis: Your produce goes straight to the people looking for it, with no middleman and no markup.
landing.kome_1_poenta: Every bit of your effort is recorded and seen.
landing.kome_2_opis: People where you live see what you do and recommend you for work you have actually done.
landing.kome_2_poenta: Do one job well, and the whole neighbourhood knows.
landing.kome_3_opis: You know how to repair, advise, teach. What you give is recorded, so later it is easier to get what you need.
landing.kome_3_poenta: Your experience becomes visible and sought after.
landing.kome_4_opis: Preserves, baking, handmade goods — everything made at home has someone nearby looking for it.
landing.kome_4_poenta: Work done at home becomes visible as a contribution to the community.
landing.kome_5_opis: Childcare, healthy food, a hand around the house — from people you know, or people known to someone you trust.
landing.kome_5_poenta: You don't have to manage alone, because we are here for each other.
landing.kome_6_naslov: Young people and those just starting out
landing.kome_6_opis: Your first people to work for, and room to show what you can do. You need neither capital nor a company, just someone to give you the first chance.
landing.kome_6_poenta: A reason to stay here, and a place you can shape.
landing.kome_7_naslov: People who care about their own area
landing.kome_7_opis: When you exchange with someone nearby, the value stays in the area instead of going somewhere far away.
landing.kome_7_poenta: Every exchange in your neighbourhood is one more connection in the network.
landing.kome_8_opis: You are already organised and you already have people. KOLO adds a record of exchange and a link to other cooperatives and individuals.
landing.kome_8_poenta: Your members join the whole network, and you gain a tool for your work.
landing.kome_9_opis: The code is open under AGPL-3.0, the content under CC BY-SA 4.0. You can check how the system works and propose changes.
landing.kome_9_poenta: A project you can trust because you can read it.
landing.primer_korak_1_naslov: Ana and Milan meet through an exchange
landing.primer_korak_1_opis: Milan needs honey, Ana produces it. Ana gave him five jars, and Milan re-registered 4,000 POEN to her, the amount the two of them agreed on.
landing.primer_korak_2_opis: Ana's washing machine broke down. Lazar repaired it, and Ana re-registered 4,000 POEN to him. She paid nothing in money, and Lazar now has a record of his work.

landing.ko_stoji_opis_2: KOLO is our version of the social and solidarity economy, adapted to Serbian law. It is an approach in which people organise themselves to care for one another, and both the United Nations and the European Union have recognised it as an equal part of the economy.
landing.ko_stoji_citat: “Every day in my surgery I see people the system ought to help but can't. Everyone has something to contribute. All they need is a tool and people around them.”

oNama.meta_title: Who stands behind KOLO — KOLO Foundation
oNama.meta_desc: Nikola Šarić, a doctor from Sombor, has spent fifteen years building a system for exchanging work, goods and knowledge without intermediaries. The story of KOLO, of the Foundation, and of how you join.
oNama.hero_podnaslov: Nikola Šarić, a doctor from Sombor
oNama.hero_opis: A system I have spent fifteen years building between people, without intermediaries. This is the story of how it came about, where it stands now, and how you join.
oNama.citat_tekst: As a doctor, my calling is to help people. I believe the society we live in is arranged for the same reason. Every day in my surgery I see people the system ought to help but cannot. Farmers, pensioners, mothers, people who are ill and who still have a great deal to give. Everyone has their place in society and something to contribute. All they need is the infrastructure — the tools and a community behind them.
oNama.prica_p1: The first doubt came back at medical school. I saw how far the incentives in the profession — from the pharmaceutical industry to the way it is funded — and regulatory policy push medicine towards treating consequences rather than preserving health. I later recognised the same logic in food production, in the economy and in the labour market. I finished medicine because I concluded that a system is easier to change from within.
oNama.prica_p2: Alongside medicine I spent years studying complementary economic systems — networks in which people exchange work and goods without money as an intermediary. In March 2014 I was a guest on the programme Na rubu znanosti on Croatian public television, in the episode on alternative currencies, where I presented ALVA, the project's form at the time. In June 2016 I spent a week on Pelion in Greece, at the Innovation in Exchange and Finance workshop at the Kalikalos school, led by Thomas Greco, author of The End of Money and the Future of Civilization and one of the best-known theorists of complementary currencies in the world.
oNama.prica_p2b: The group also included the team from Volos, who ran Volos TEM, a Greek exchange network born at the height of the debt crisis. People there exchange food, services and craft goods at markets of their own, recording value instead of paying it. At its best the network had more than 800 members. I put the same subjects forward at home too, at public talks in Stanišić, Sombor, Novi Sad and Belgrade.
oNama.prica_p3: Over the years the idea changed name and form: ALVA in 2012, Transition Alternative in 2013, the Alva Foundation in 2016. Today it is KOLO. After fifteen years we have finished documentation, a registered Foundation and a platform that works. The structure is set up so that in time it runs ever more independently of any one person, myself included.
oNama.status_opis: The system is being built in phases. The first is behind us; we are in the second now.
oNama.faza1_opis: Platform built, documentation written, Foundation registered. (Behind us.)
oNama.faza2_opis: Real users check the whole flow under real conditions: registration, proof of reality, POEN, the Marketplace and the programmes.
oNama.faza3_opis: Public registration opens. The goal is to reach enough confirmed people for exchange and mutuality in the first community to sustain themselves.
oNama.faza4_opis: All modules are running, including cooperatives and support programmes, and shared decision-making goes through the Upper Kolo. The community governs the system itself.
oNama.faza5_opis: Cooperatives are founded in several cities and connected into a network. KOLO is no longer tied to a single place.
oNama.faza6_opis: KOLO rests entirely on existing law. In this phase the model also gains a formally recognised place in the legal framework, through legislation and a clear positioning of the model.
oNama.faza7_opis: Through mutual aid the community itself carries what is today left to institutions or to no one: security when it is needed, care for the ill and the elderly, the passing on of knowledge, food production, mutual financing and shared decision-making.
oNama.otvaranje_opis: We are checking the whole flow in practice, with real people and real exchange. Nothing here is a simulation.
oNama.stavka1_tekst: The whole path a user goes through: registration, proof of reality through the chain, recording, re-registering and writing off POEN, the Marketplace, the programmes and donations.
oNama.stavka2_tekst: We check that every record holds: the balance of accounts, the nightly calculations and the record of contributions. The aim is for the figures to be right down to the last POEN.
oNama.stavka3_tekst: We look for mistakes and possible abuse now, while the network is small and the damage would be small. That is the only moment when it can be done cheaply.
oNama.stavka4_tekst: Everything you enter stays. Your account, your POEN, the contributions recorded and the history of your exchanges carry over into the next phase. This testing is not a trial run that gets wiped.
oNama.stavka5_tekst: When the platform is stable and the whole flow runs without errors, we move into Critical mass and open public registration. The opening does not depend on the number of POEN; that threshold comes later, with the Upper Kolo.
oNama.stavka6_tekst: The KOLO Foundation is entered in the Register of Endowments and Foundations at the Serbian Business Registers Agency, with its seat in Sombor. The registration details are further down this page.
oNama.ukljucivanje_naslov: The system is built through different forms of contribution
oNama.ukljucivanje_opis: Whether you have five minutes, knowledge, means or an acquaintance, there is a way to help.
oNama.istaknut_naslov: Come in and see how it works
oNama.istaknut_tekst: The most important contribution asks for neither a company nor special knowledge. Registration takes a minute, and you get access straight away and see the whole system from the inside. When it seems worth it to you, invite the people you know — neighbours, friends, relatives.
oNama.k1_tekst: The first members lay the foundations of the community, and their work in that early phase is recognised in particular through the operational contribution, which is governed by a separate rulebook. The system is already open and exchange is already happening.
oNama.k2_tekst: If you run a company or are able to support the development, a donation to the Foundation covers the cost of maintaining the platform and running the system. Patrons are listed publicly. A donation is a separate act and buys nothing inside the system; everything that follows from it is governed by the Rulebook on Patronage and Donations.
oNama.k3_tekst: If you are a developer, a designer, or work in another IT field, we need help with the platform. The software is open under AGPL-3.0, so you can look at the code before you get in touch. Even a few hours a month is useful.
oNama.sek1_tekst: Writers, journalists, editors, video producers and designers, as well as academics in economics, law, sociology and anthropology. What we need most is someone who can translate complex ideas into language a farmer, a pensioner and a twenty-year-old all understand. Criticism from within strengthens the system as much as support does.
oNama.sek2_tekst: Experience in running a company, an association or a larger organisation. The Foundation is entering a phase in which operations grow faster than one person, and we need coordination between the Management Board and the executive functions.
oNama.sek3_tekst: Lawyers with an interest in cooperative law, foundation law and questions around digital platforms, as well as accountants with experience in the non-profit sector.
oNama.sek4_tekst: Contacts in the cooperative movement, producer associations, trade unions, civil society and local government. All of it speeds up the spread of the system where it makes the most sense.
oNama.sek5_naslov: A room for a public talk
oNama.sek5_tekst: If you can provide a room for a talk, a presentation or a smaller gathering in your town, get in touch. Sombor and its surroundings come first, but every town in Serbia and the region is welcome.
oNama.sek6_tekst: Individuals can be donors to the Foundation too. A donation is a separate act and buys nothing inside the system; everything that follows from it is governed by the Rulebook on Patronage and Donations.

oNama.stub1_tekst: The Foundation is the legal footing of the system. It receives donations and patronage in money, goods and services, covers the cost of the platform, holds the infrastructure, and speaks on KOLO's behalf before the state and its institutions. The Foundation distributes no profit; everything it receives goes back into the system.

oNama.stub3_tekst: The Management Board takes strategic decisions and the director runs operations. Once the community activates the Upper Kolo, its body for shared decision-making, the Foundation stops deciding and starts executing: it carries out decisions and answers every recommendation of the Upper Kolo with reasons, in public.

oSistemu.meta_title: Where KOLO comes from — solidarity economy in practice
oSistemu.meta_desc: Systems in which people exchange work, goods and knowledge through a ledger of their own have been running in Switzerland since 1934, in Canada since 1983, in Sardinia and in Japan. KOLO belongs to that family.
oSistemu.hero_opis: What KOLO records, how it is set up, and which tradition it comes from.
oSistemu.zajednicko_citat: “Grain by grain, a loaf; stone by stone, a palace.”
oSistemu.zajednicko_p1: Acquaintances, work, knowledge, goods, time and the infrastructure the Foundation maintains all pass through KOLO. All of it leaves a trace: it strengthens the network, the knowledge and the trust, and those remain available to everyone. The community thereby becomes more capable of caring for itself.
oSistemu.zajednicko_p2_post: . It is no one's property, yet it is everyone's care: the rules are shared, and it is maintained by those who use it.
oSistemu.zajednicko_p3_pre: is a record of your contribution to the common good. An acknowledgement that you brought something, and the mark by which others in the network know you.
oSistemu.svg_cuva_ime: which the Foundation holds and, under the Statute, uses for the community
oSistemu.svg_svi_zajedno: all users together form the KOLO Community
oSistemu.svg_nosioci_odlucuju: ZRNO Holders decide through the Upper Kolo
oSistemu.svg_zerosum: · the sum of all records is zero
oSistemu.k1_tekst: Everyone who has accepted KOLO's rules. Through their work, goods and knowledge they contribute to the common good, and that is recorded for them in POEN. Whoever holds ZRNO also takes part in decisions through the Upper Kolo.
oSistemu.k2_tekst: It is made up of all ZRNO holders, and its composition changes with every accounting period. It decides by quadratic voting: the number of votes is the square root of the number of active ZRNO, so someone with a hundred ZRNO has ten votes. That is what keeps power from ending up with a handful of people.
oSistemu.k3_podnaslov: the software that keeps the record
oSistemu.k3_tekst: It is open under AGPL-3.0, which means anyone may read, use and improve it, while changes must stay equally open. The Foundation maintains and runs it. It records POEN and keeps the ledger under rules that are set in advance, public and the same for everyone. With every POEN recorded it records the same amount against itself as a minus, so the sum of all records stays zero.
oSistemu.k4_podnaslov: the legal entity behind the system
oSistemu.k4_tekst: A foundation registered in Sombor. It receives donations and patronage in dinars, goods and services, covers the cost of running the system, holds the infrastructure and represents KOLO before the community and the state. The Statute and the Rulebook bind it to use all of that for the common good.
oSistemu.topla_voda_tag: We are not reinventing the wheel
oSistemu.topla_voda_naslov: This already works elsewhere, and has for decades
oSistemu.topla_voda_p1: The idea that a community can organise its own exchange is not new. Nor is it exotic. In various countries people have for decades been exchanging work, goods and knowledge through ledgers of their own, with a unit that is not money yet makes exchange within the network possible.
oSistemu.topla_voda_p2_post: , and it covers cooperatives, foundations and mutual societies — organisations that work for a social purpose, decide democratically and return value to the community. The field has been formally recognised by the International Labour Organization, the United Nations General Assembly, and the Council and the Commission of the European Union.
oSistemu.topla_voda_p3: KOLO is one attempt within that field, adapted to Serbian law and to the needs here. It does not present itself as a finished product: the rules change through participation and democratic procedure, and they will keep changing as the network grows.
oSistemu.sistemi_opis: Four networks from different parts of the world. Different countries, different contexts — but the same family of systems. KOLO belongs to that family, with its own distinctive features.
oSistemu.sistemi_wir_opis: The oldest system of its kind still running today. Founded in 1934, at the height of the Great Depression, as a mutual credit network among businesses. Every member starts from zero and repays by selling to other members. The WIR franc is not exchanged for Swiss francs. Today more than fifty thousand Swiss small and medium businesses trade within the network.
oSistemu.sistemi_wir_pokazao: A mutual credit network can last ninety years and be countercyclical. When the official economy weakens, trade within WIR grows.
oSistemu.sistemi_lets_opis: In the early eighties, in a small town on Vancouver Island, Michael Linton started the first Local Exchange Trading System — a local network in which members exchange work, goods and services using a ledger unit of their own, unconnected to the national currency. A typical LETS network gathers anywhere from a few dozen to a few hundred people, and the sum of all accounts is always zero. In Britain there were five such networks in 1992, and about 350 three years later, with tens of thousands of members.
oSistemu.sistemi_lets_pokazao: The model spreads fast and needs no expensive technology. But it also showed the limit: networks that stay small and go unused day to day fade away in time. Durability does not come from the idea, but from how often it is used.
oSistemu.sistemi_sardex_opis: Started in 2010 as a response to the debt crisis that hit Sardinia hard. A group of young Sardinians, with little experience in finance or business but a clear grasp of their region's problem, built a mutual credit network among local companies. Every member starts from zero, the sum of all accounts is always zero, and there is no interest.
oSistemu.sistemi_sardex_pokazao: A local team, with no large investment and no state support, can build a durable network in about ten years — given persistence, structure, and an understanding of the real problems of the place.
oSistemu.sistemi_fureai_opis: A Japanese exchange system based on time and care for the elderly. Members who help older people — through home care, accompaniment, cooking — log the hours worked and can use them for themselves or transfer them to a family member elsewhere in the country who cares for their own parent. It grew into hundreds of organisations with around a hundred thousand users across Japan, operating in parallel with the state care system for years.
oSistemu.sistemi_fureai_pokazao: A contribution ledger can become the infrastructure of care for vulnerable groups in society. Recognising care work as economically measurable does not degrade its human character — on the contrary, it makes it visible and transferable.
oSistemu.familija_naslov: The same family, with its own distinctive features
oSistemu.familija_p1: KOLO is not a copy of any of those networks. They built a unit for exchange. KOLO builds a record of contribution, and exchange is what follows from it.
oSistemu.familija_p2: What those networks do not have is a chain of confirmations. In KOLO the reality of every member is confirmed by someone who knows them personally and answers for it. That is what keeps the network real.
oSistemu.familija_p3_pre: The second difference is that contribution and voice are not mixed.
oSistemu.familija_p3_zrno: carries the vote in decisions, with quadratic voting that keeps power from ending up with a handful of people. Support for mothers, the elderly and pupils is not an add-on but part of the system.
oSistemu.familija_p4: The third difference is what rests on what. What you agree and hand over to each other is the exchange. POEN is only a record of it. A record on its own obliges no one to anything.
oSistemu.familija_p5: There are also differences that are easy to check. WIR obtained a banking licence in 1936 because it lends to its members, while KOLO does not lend. Sardex is a company that charges an annual membership fee, while entering KOLO is free. Neither of those approaches is wrong — they are answers to a different problem.
oSistemu.familija_p6: With all of that, KOLO belongs to the same family: systems that record exchange between people, run alongside official money, and work for their users instead of using them.
oSistemu.okvir_opis: In recent years the social and solidarity economy has gained what it lacked for decades: an agreed definition, a United Nations resolution and a European Union action plan. None of them mentions KOLO, and KOLO did not come out of them. These documents describe a field that fits KOLO — and it is the field Serbia is taking on through accession.
oSistemu.okvir1_naslov: European Union · Social Economy Action Plan
oSistemu.okvir1_tekst: A plan with 63 actions and a horizon to 2030. It defines the social economy through three features: the primacy of people and of social or environmental purpose over profit, the reinvestment of most profits and surpluses in the collective or general interest, and democratic or participatory governance. Among the models it names platform cooperatives, and among the measures the strengthening of grassroots initiatives.
oSistemu.okvir2_naslov: International Labour Organization · Resolution on decent work and the social and solidarity economy
oSistemu.okvir2_tekst: The first internationally agreed definition, adopted tripartitely by governments, employers and trade unions from 187 states. Alongside democratic governance and the primacy of people over capital, it names voluntary cooperation, mutual aid and autonomy.
oSistemu.okvir3_naslov: United Nations · General Assembly, Resolution A/RES/77/281
oSistemu.okvir3_tekst: The first General Assembly resolution on this field. It calls on states to develop legal and financial frameworks for it. The series continued with a resolution in 2024.
oSistemu.okvir4_naslov: European Union · Council Recommendation on the conditions for the social economy to thrive
oSistemu.okvir4_tekst: An elaboration of the Action Plan. It calls on member states to adopt national strategies, and among the priorities it names short food supply chains.
oSistemu.pristup_tekst_pre: Serbia is negotiating accession, so this framework concerns it too — formally through
oSistemu.pristup_tekst_bold: chapter 19, social policy and employment, and chapter 22, regional policy
oSistemu.pristup_tekst_post: . None of these documents is a binding regulation. They are definitions, recommendations and plans, and their value lies in showing which way things are going.
oSistemu.prema_p1: KOLO is not at the start of that road. The features from both definitions are already built into how the system works; they are not goals still to be reached.
oSistemu.prema_p2: The rules are decided by ZRNO holders, through quadratic voting, and the rules are public and change by the same procedure for everyone. The Foundation distributes no profit and returns everything to the system. POEN is not an object of trade. Participation is voluntary, and support for mothers, the elderly and pupils is built into the mechanism itself. The software is open under AGPL-3.0, so anyone can check how it works.
oSistemu.prema_p3: This is not an endorsement from anyone. It means there is a yardstick against which KOLO can be checked.
oSistemu.zasto_p1: Bačka has one of the oldest cooperative traditions in Europe. The Gazdovský spolok, founded in 1846 in Bački Petrovac, two years after the Rochdale cooperative in England, is still cited among the first cooperatives in the world. Cooperatives, homesteads, lending a hand in the fields: this is not history that needs explaining here — older people in the villages around Sombor remember it first-hand. KOLO does not introduce a new form of organising, but the one that used to be ordinary in these parts.
oSistemu.zasto_p2: Sombor is large enough for the effects of a network to show, and small enough to see who is producing them. A town ringed by homesteads and villages means the craftsman, the pensioner, the housewife, the young mother and the farmer are all in the same place. It also means that those of us building this live here, so whatever does not work is not something we can fail to notice.
oSistemu.zasto_citat: One hand washes the other, and both wash the face.
oSistemu.cta_opis: Now that you know where the system comes from,
oSistemu.cta_opis2: what is left is to see how it works.

kakoFunkcionisePage.meta_title: How KOLO works, step by step
kakoFunkcionisePage.meta_desc: How you enter KOLO, how it is confirmed that you are a real person, how POEN comes about and who decides on the rules. A detailed explanation of the whole system.
kakoFunkcionisePage.hero_opis: An explanation of the whole system. The shorter version is on the home page.
kakoFunkcionisePage.k1_opis: An email, a nickname and a password, and that is all. No ID card is needed, nor any other document. Throughout the interface others see you only under your nickname, while your real name, phone number and location are entered only if you decide to, and you can remove them at any time. Registration is free.
kakoFunkcionisePage.k2_naslov: What you can do straight away
kakoFunkcionisePage.k2_opis: You see the public record of exchanges and every listing on the Marketplace, with its content, price and place. You can post your first three listings and exchange, and POEN can be re-registered to you. Until you are confirmed you cannot re-register POEN to someone else yourself, post a request, or write to advertisers first. That is why the first step is usually your own listing, which someone already in the network responds to.
kakoFunkcionisePage.k3_naslov: Confirmation through the chain of confirmations
kakoFunkcionisePage.k3_opis:
A full member who knows you personally confirms that you are a real person. Through that confirmation you both enter the chain of confirmations, and the Protocol — the software that keeps the record — records 1,000 POEN for each of you.
Every confirmation raises your reality index by 10 per cent. You can receive ten confirmations in total, and you yourself can confirm anyone who is not already in your chain.
kakoFunkcionisePage.k4_opis: Now you have full access: you post listings without limit, ask for what you need, re-register POEN, contribute to the system and apply for the programmes. You too can bring in and confirm people you personally know.
kakoFunkcionisePage.k5_opis: ZRNO gives you the right to vote in the Upper Kolo, the body of ZRNO holders that decides on the rules applying to everyone. Votes are counted by square root, so no one with a lot of ZRNO can outvote the community on their own.
kakoFunkcionisePage.odgovornost_tekst: Whoever confirms someone who is not a real person loses those 1,000 POEN. For abuse they lose the right to confirm anyone further, and for a repeated one they may be excluded from the network. That is why a confirmation in KOLO is worth something.
kakoFunkcionisePage.evidencija_naslov: Seven channels through which the Protocol records POEN in your ledger
kakoFunkcionisePage.poen_ne_kupuje: POEN is not bought for money.
kakoFunkcionisePage.poen_kanali: It is recorded through seven channels of contribution, under rules that are public and the same for everyone. For exchange, confirmation and donation the recording is automatic. For work for the community and for patronage, someone must first confirm that the work was done.
kakoFunkcionisePage.poen_preraspodela: When you exchange with someone, POEN is only re-registered from one to the other. Existing records are redistributed and nothing new comes into being.
kakoFunkcionisePage.n1_opis: Your first listing offering a good or a service — with a photograph, a description, a category and a place — brings you 1,000 POEN.
kakoFunkcionisePage.poen_jeste1: A record of what you have given to the community
kakoFunkcionisePage.poen_jeste2: It does not expire — your contribution is remembered for good
kakoFunkcionisePage.poen_jeste3: It is re-registered to someone else when you exchange
kakoFunkcionisePage.poen_jeste4: The basis on which ZRNO is recorded
kakoFunkcionisePage.poen_nije_uvod: In short: POEN is not money, it is not bought for dinars, and trading in it is forbidden by the Rulebook. The legal reasons are set out below.
kakoFunkcionisePage.poen_nije3: Digital assets or a cryptocurrency (Law on Digital Assets)
kakoFunkcionisePage.poen_nije4: A financial instrument or an investment scheme (Capital Markets Law)
kakoFunkcionisePage.poen_nije5: A claim against the Foundation or a property right of the user
kakoFunkcionisePage.poen_nije6: A thing existing outside the ledger — POEN is a record and nothing else
kakoFunkcionisePage.zerosum_naslov: How POEN comes about and how it moves
kakoFunkcionisePage.zerosum_tekst:
New POEN comes about only through the seven channels of contribution. Every time the Protocol records new POEN, it records the same amount against itself as a minus, so the sum of all records in the system — those of users and those of the Protocol — is always exactly zero.
In an exchange between people nothing new comes about. POEN is only re-registered from one to the other.
kakoFunkcionisePage.zrno_uvod: ZRNO gives you a vote in the Upper Kolo, the body that decides on KOLO's rules. Whoever contributes over a long time also gains a say in what the system looks like.
kakoFunkcionisePage.zrno_upis1: You record ZRNO yourself, on the basis of the POEN you have already gathered.
kakoFunkcionisePage.zrno_upis2: The total quantity of ZRNO is fixed at 1,000,000, and that number never changes.
kakoFunkcionisePage.zrno_upis3: How much POEN one ZRNO takes is set by the accounting coefficient, which rises as the amount of POEN in circulation rises.
kakoFunkcionisePage.zrno_upis4: ZRNO is not transferred between users. It stays with whoever recorded it.
kakoFunkcionisePage.zrno_koristi1: Active ZRNO gives you a vote in the Upper Kolo and cannot be written off while it is active.
kakoFunkcionisePage.zrno_koristi2: The number of votes is the square root of the number of active ZRNO. Someone with a hundred ZRNO has ten votes, not a hundred. That is why no one can outvote the community alone, however many they hold.
kakoFunkcionisePage.zrno_koristi4: You can hand your votes to another ZRNO holder — the votes only, never the ZRNO.
kakoFunkcionisePage.zrno_koristi5: Free ZRNO can be written off back to the Protocol, giving you POEN at the current coefficient.
kakoFunkcionisePage.koeficijent_naslov: The accounting coefficient is not an exchange rate
kakoFunkcionisePage.koeficijent_tekst:
The accounting coefficient is the ratio between the POEN recorded and the ZRNO available. It says only how much POEN one ZRNO takes at a given moment.
Since the coefficient rises as the network grows, whoever recorded ZRNO earlier receives more POEN on writing it off later than they gave for it. That is a recognition of those who held the system up while it was small.
This is not earnings. Writing off ZRNO gives you POEN, and POEN is not money, is not exchanged for dinars and does not leave the system. The coefficient is not a price and does not express the value of ZRNO outside KOLO.
kakoFunkcionisePage.cta_naslov: Now you know how it works
kakoFunkcionisePage.cta_opis: All that is left is to join. Registration takes about a minute, and right after it you can post your first three listings and see who is around you. Confirmation comes through your first exchange.
kakoFunkcionisePage.cta_licence: Software: AGPL-3.0 · Content: CC BY-SA 4.0 · Common good and licences
kakoFunkcionisePage.n7_opis:
Recognition for the founders for what was invested before the system even existed: years of developing the concept and the documentation, building the platform, and the material costs they bore themselves, without a single dinar in compensation.
The channel is limited both in amount and in pace. It is recorded in steps of 24,000 POEN, at most one step for every 100,000 POEN in the system, so it cannot be sped up. It closes permanently at 2,400,000 POEN.
kakoFunkcionisePage.n6_opis:
You donate money to the Foundation, and the Protocol records POEN for you at a coefficient that rises with your total contribution.
POEN from a donation grants no ownership, does not turn into money and does not buy votes. A vote depends on ZRNO, and voting is quadratic, so a larger donor cannot outvote the community.
The terms are the same for everyone: the same table, the same thresholds, the same coefficients. An anonymous donation carries no POEN.
kakoFunkcionisePage.n5_opis:
A legal entity or a sole trader — a company, an association or a shop — signs a donation contract with the Foundation, in money, goods or services. The patron itself receives no POEN. The recognition is recorded for the owner who is a full member, or for the sole trader themselves, according to a table of seven levels.
The network needs money in order to run, and the terms of patronage are the same for every legal entity.
kakoFunkcionisePage.n4_opis: Programmes for mothers and carers, the elderly, special care and schooling, in which approved users have POEN recorded every day. This is not social assistance in the sense of the law and does not affect any entitlements you have from the state.
kakoFunkcionisePage.n3_opis: Concrete work for the community. ZRNO holders — in the first phase the Foundation's Management Board — publish a task, you apply and carry it out, then they confirm it was done, and only then is POEN recorded.
kakoFunkcionisePage.n2_opis: When a full member who knows you personally confirms you in the chain of confirmations, the Protocol records 1,000 POEN for you and 1,000 for them. When the confirmation is subject to oversight, 500 POEN goes to the overseer as well.

dobrodosli.ekran1_p1: In KOLO people exchange goods, services and help without money.
dobrodosli.ekran1_p2: Your account is open, but still locked. It unlocks when someone who knows you personally confirms that you are a real person.
dobrodosli.ekran1_p3: Depending on whether you already know someone in KOLO, choose one of the next two steps. You can reopen this guide any time from the „?” at the top.
dobrodosli.ekran1_p4: On a computer the menu with all pages sits on the left-hand side; on a phone it opens with the ☰ icon in the top left corner. Every instruction in this guide also shows where that page is.
dobrodosli.ekran2_naslov: Do you know someone already in KOLO?
dobrodosli.ekran2_p1: Open Confirmation and click „Show code”. You will get a QR code and a six-digit number.
dobrodosli.ekran2_p2: Show them the QR in person or send them the six-digit number in a message. On their side they open Confirmation, click „Confirm someone” and scan or type in that number. That makes you a full member.
dobrodosli.ekran2_p3: The code is valid for 2 hours. If it expires, make a new one with the same button. The moment they confirm you, you get 1,000 POEN and full access.
dobrodosli.ekran3_p1: Then post what you offer on the Marketplace. You can put up your first three listings right away, without a single confirmation — that is how people from your area see you.
dobrodosli.ekran3_p2: The fields are: first name, last name, year of birth, place, nickname and what you do. All are optional, but do enter at least your name and place, so that the card can be shown to people around you.
dobrodosli.ekran3_p3: Your listing stays up until you take it down. Whoever recognises you gets in touch about the listing — and can confirm that you are real.
dobrodosli.ekran3_p4: Also leave your phone number with consent. If nobody recognises you within those 8 days, a member of the Foundation's Board will call you. Only the Board can see the number, and it is deleted as soon as you are confirmed or the card expires.
dobrodosli.ekran4_naslov: What you get the moment someone confirms you
dobrodosli.ekran4_p1: One confirmation is enough and takes your reality index to 10%, which is exactly the threshold for full access.
dobrodosli.ekran4_p2: You immediately receive 1,000 POEN, and this unlocks: posting listings on the marketplace, contacting advertisers, messages, writing in the community chat, pseudonyms in the records, subscribing ZRNO and applying to programmes.
dobrodosli.ekran4_p3: You also become a link in the chain of confirmations: from that moment you can confirm people you personally know.
dobrodosli.ekran5_p1: POEN is a record of contribution — it notes what you gave and what you received in the network. It is not money: it cannot be bought, cannot be exchanged for dinars and has no value outside the system.
dobrodosli.ekran5_p2: For example: you fix a neighbour's tap, they re-register those POEN into your record; later you get honey from a third person for them. How much POEN an exchange is worth — the two of you agree.
dobrodosli.ekran5_p3: For now POEN arrives in three ways: 1,000 for your first listing offering a good or a service — once the Foundation approves it; 1,000 when someone confirms you; and whatever you agree on in each exchange.
dobrodosli.ekran6_naslov: What you can do right away, before confirmation
dobrodosli.ekran6_p1: While you wait for someone to confirm you, there are two things you can do right away.
dobrodosli.ekran6_p2: First, set up your profile: add a photo, your name, location and a few words about yourself. For each field you choose whether others can see it. This is what people see when you contact them, so an account without a photo gets a weaker response. The switch for email notifications is there too.
dobrodosli.ekran6_p3: Editing your profile does not affect confirmation. Recognition uses your Marketplace listing, not your profile.
dobrodosli.ekran6_p4: Second, open the marketplace and look at what people are offering and looking for. Browsing listings is open to everyone, without confirmation. Follow the Foundation's news on the home page too: announcements, rule changes and everything important for the community go there.
dobrodosli.ekran6_p5: You can post an offer straight away, before confirmation — for your first such listing you receive 1,000 POEN once the Foundation approves it. Confirmation unlocks want-ads, contacting an advertiser and starting a conversation.
dobrodosli.ekran7_p1: If you know someone in KOLO, open Confirmation, click „Show code” and send it to them. If you don't know anyone, post an offer on the Marketplace and wait for someone to get in touch. Either takes a couple of minutes.
dobrodosli.ekran7_p2: When someone confirms you, a notification arrives in the bell and by email.

Members without a confirmation are skipped — you approve those one by one in the First listings tab. Those whose contribution was recorded without a notification going out are notified as well.
